mk:ls-news-1.text: A city in the Netherlands has become the first in Europe to ban private cars from its historic centre. From next January, only residents, delivery vans and emergency vehicles will be allowed inside the old town. The city council says the move follows a two-year trial in which air pollution in the area fell by nearly a third and the number of shoppers rose by 12 percent. Shop owners were initially opposed, fearing a loss of customers, but most now support the plan. The council will spend 40 million euros on bike parking and electric buses, and it expects the ban to cut traffic accidents in the centre by half.

mk:ls-news-2.text: A study of 12,000 adults over the age of 60 has found that those who walked for at least 30 minutes a day were 20 percent less likely to develop memory problems over the following five years. The researchers, from a university in Sweden, stress that the link held even after they adjusted for age, education and smoking. They say the effect may come from improved blood flow to the brain rather than from the exercise being enjoyable. The team warns, however, that the study only shows an association and cannot prove that walking protects memory.

mk:ls-conv-1.text: W: Hi Tom, you look exhausted. Did you stay up for the match last night? M: Don't remind me. I set my alarm for two in the morning, watched the whole thing, and we lost in the last five minutes. W: Ouch. But aren't you presenting your project today? M: At three. I've got six hours to finish the slides. Actually, the data's all there — it's the design that's killing me. W: I did mine last week. If you send me the file, I can put it into the template we were given. It only takes twenty minutes. M: Really? That would save me. But I don't want to take up your lunch break. W: I'm free until one. And you can buy me coffee afterwards.

mk:ls-pass-1.text: Every Saturday morning in a community hall in Bristol, a dozen volunteers sit behind tables with screwdrivers, soldering irons and sewing machines. This is a repair café, part of a movement that began in Amsterdam in 2009 and has since spread to more than 2,000 places worldwide. Visitors bring broken toasters, lamps, bicycles and clothes; the volunteers, many of them retired engineers, try to fix them for free. The idea is not only to keep things out of landfill. Organisers say the real value is the conversation: people learn how their possessions work, and they leave with a reason to mend rather than replace. Roughly seven in ten items are successfully repaired.

mk:ls-news-3.text: A university in Manchester has opened what it calls a student-run laboratory, where undergraduates design and carry out their own experiments instead of following set recipes. The lab, housed in a former storeroom, cost about 60,000 pounds to convert and is equipped with second-hand instruments donated by local firms. In its first year, 240 students used the space, and 17 of their projects were later published in student journals. The head of the chemistry department says the aim is not to produce researchers but to teach students how to fail usefully. About half of the experiments do not work the first time, and students must write a short report explaining what went wrong. The university plans to open a second lab next September and to admit first-year students, a group that was previously excluded.

mk:ls-news-4.text: The Dutch city of Rotterdam has turned an underground car park into a giant water tank. The tank can hold 10,000 cubic metres of rainwater, roughly the amount that falls on the district during a heavy storm. It cost 30 million euros and was completed after three years of work. When the tank fills up, the water is pumped slowly into the river once the storm has passed. Four hundred parking spaces were lost in the process, and residents were initially angry about it. The city argues that the tank is used only two or three times a year, and that on all other days the space works as a normal car park. Engineers say the project has already prevented flooding in more than 60 basements since it opened.

mk:ls-news-5.text: A survey of 1,200 employers in Britain suggests that most companies now rely on software to read job applications. Sixty-eight percent of those questioned said the software decides which CVs reach a human reader, yet only 12 percent believed the results were completely reliable. The survey also found that applications with tables, photographs or unusual fonts are more likely to be rejected, because the software cannot read them properly. Researchers advise candidates to use simple layouts and standard headings, and to repeat key words from the job advertisement. They warn, however, that the practice may hide good candidates who describe their skills in an unfamiliar way.

mk:ls-conv-2.text: M: Good morning, Professor Lane. I am here about two things, if you have a minute. The research methods course clashes with my statistics class on Tuesday mornings. W: Let me look. There is a second group on Thursday afternoons, but it is already full. I can put you on the waiting list, though I should warn you that only about five people usually get in. M: I see. Then I may have to take statistics next term instead. The other thing is my dissertation. I would like to write about food waste in supermarkets. W: That topic is far too broad for eight thousand words. Pick one store, measure what it throws away for four weeks, and you will have something original. M: The problem is access. Most stores will not let a student go through their bins. W: True. I can write a letter on department paper. That usually helps. But the proposal deadline is the fifteenth, so tell me by Friday whether you want to go ahead. M: I will email you on Thursday. Thank you.

mk:ls-conv-3.text: W: Hello, is that Daniel? I am calling about the flat on Mill Road, the one-bedroom on the second floor. M: Yes, hello. I saw the advert this morning. Could you tell me what the rent includes? W: It is 480 pounds a month, and that covers water and rubbish collection. Electricity and heating are separate, about 40 pounds a month in winter. M: Right. And how far is it from the campus? W: It is about two miles. Most students take the number 14 bus, which stops at the corner and takes fifteen minutes. Cycling is quicker, but the road is busy. M: I do not have a bike, so the bus is fine. When could I see it? W: I am showing three people round on Saturday morning. If you like it, you can sign the contract the same day, and the deposit is one month's rent. M: Saturday works for me. Should I bring anything? W: Just your passport and a letter from your university.

mk:ls-pass-2.text: Why do we forget something we learned yesterday but remember a song from childhood? Part of the answer lies in what happens while we sleep. During deep sleep, the brain replays the patterns it produced during the day, and moves information from short-term storage into longer-term networks. In one experiment, students learned a list of forty words in the evening. Half were allowed eight hours of sleep, while the other half were woken after five. The next morning, the well-rested group recalled about twenty percent more words, and their brains showed stronger links between the word list and existing knowledge. The researchers point out that the amount of sleep matters less than its timing: a short nap of twenty minutes after studying can also help, provided it comes soon after learning. They suggest that students review difficult material in the evening rather than late at night, and avoid staying up to cram before an exam.

mk:ls-pass-3.text: The idea of the fifteen-minute city is simple: everything you need for daily life should be within a fifteen-minute walk or cycle of your home. Schools, shops, clinics, parks and workplaces would all sit close together, so that residents no longer depend on a car. Paris has been the most visible test case. Since 2020, the city has turned dozens of parking areas into small gardens and playgrounds, and opened school yards to the public at weekends. Supporters say the model cuts traffic and strengthens neighbourhood life. Critics point out that the people who benefit most are those who can afford to live in the centre; when a district becomes more pleasant, rents rise and lower-income families are pushed to the edges. The city replies that a fifth of its social housing is being built in these same districts. Early data show that car journeys inside the centre have fallen by around a quarter since the project began.

mk:cr-1.text: A street tree does more than shade a pavement. In a heatwave, a mature plane tree can lower the air temperature beneath its crown by as much as five degrees, simply by releasing water vapour through its leaves and by blocking sunlight before it reaches the ground. This is not a small detail in cities that are already several degrees warmer than the countryside around them. The problem is that the trees most able to do this are the ones that take longest to grow. A newly planted sapling with a trunk the width of a wrist provides almost no shade, and it will be twenty or thirty years before it earns its place. City budgets, however, are usually planned in four-year cycles, which means that planting a tree is a gift to a mayor who will not be in office to open it. Some cities have tried to solve this by planting faster-growing species, but the results have been mixed. Fast growers such as poplars reach a useful size in a decade, yet they are also the first to drop branches in a storm, and their roots tend to lift pavements, which makes them unpopular with the engineers who maintain the streets. Slower, denser species such as oaks cost more and take longer, but they survive drought better and live for centuries. A more promising approach is to stop treating trees as decoration and start treating them as infrastructure. In Melbourne, every tree now has an email address and a record of its species, age and water needs, and residents can report a dying tree the way they would report a broken streetlight. The city has also changed its accounting: the value of the shade a tree provides is now counted as a benefit, which means a tree that survives fifty years can be justified on financial grounds alone. That change of accounting may matter more than any single planting programme. A tree that is planted and then forgotten dies within five years, and a dead tree costs the city twice — once to buy and once to remove.

mk:cr-2.text: Walk into any supermarket and you will find dates printed on almost everything: «best before», «use by», «display until». Shoppers treat them as instructions from authority, and the result is that a third of the food thrown away in British homes is still perfectly edible. The confusion is built into the language. «Use by» is a safety date: after it, food may make you ill, and it applies mainly to fresh meat, fish and ready meals. «Best before» is a quality date: the food is still safe afterwards, it simply may not taste as good. Most shoppers do not know the difference, and surveys suggest that fewer than half can explain it correctly. Retailers have little reason to clarify. Longer shelf life sells, so manufacturers compete to print later dates, and some adjust the recipe — adding salt or removing water — to make those dates achievable. The customer gets food that lasts longer and tastes saltier. Several countries have begun to experiment. In Denmark, a chain of stores sells only goods past their «best before» date, at prices reduced by up to fifty percent, and it has been profitable for eight years. In Britain, a campaign persuaded two of the largest chains to remove «display until» dates, which existed mainly to help staff rotate stock and were never meant for customers. Within a year, the amount of food wasted in those stores fell noticeably. None of this removes the need for judgement. A date is a rule written for the average kitchen, not for yours. The useful question is not «is it out of date?» but «does it look, smell and taste right?» — which is, of course, what people did before the labels were invented.

mk:cr-3.text: In 2014 a pair of psychologists published a study that became one of the most cited findings in education. They asked students to watch lectures and take notes either by hand or on a laptop, then tested them on factual recall and on their understanding of concepts. Laptop users wrote down far more words, but the handwritten group performed better on the conceptual questions. The explanation offered was that handwriting is slower, which forces the note-taker to summarise rather than transcribe. The finding spread quickly, and with it a simple rule: ban laptops from the classroom. But replication has been unkind. When other teams repeated the experiment with different students, different lectures and different tests, the advantage of handwriting shrank, and in several studies it disappeared entirely. A 2019 review of twenty-two experiments concluded that the original result was real but narrow. Handwriting helps when the material is conceptual and the test requires explanation. It does not help when students are recalling names, dates or definitions, where the extra words typed by laptop users are an advantage rather than a distraction. There is a second issue that the debate usually ignores. What matters may not be the pen but the habit. Students who normally write by hand have practised summarising for years; students who normally type have practised something else. Asking them to switch for one lecture measures a skill they have not developed, not a tool they are using badly. The practical conclusion is less dramatic than the headline. If you are learning a subject that requires you to explain ideas, slow down and write less. If you are collecting facts, speed is not a sin.

mk:cr-4.text: Hiring algorithms are sold as a cure for bias. A human recruiter, the argument goes, is influenced by a candidate's accent, school or photograph; software judges only the words on the page. Several large employers now screen most applications this way, and the vendors of such systems advertise them as objective. The argument contains a hidden assumption: that the words on the page are neutral. They are not. A system trained on a company's past hires learns whatever pattern those hires had in common — and if the company spent the last decade hiring from three universities, the model will quietly prefer candidates from those three universities. Nothing in the code says so; the preference is inherited from the data. This is not a hypothetical risk. In 2018 a major technology firm abandoned a recruiting tool after discovering that it downgraded résumés containing the word «women's», as in «women's chess club». The model had not been told to prefer men. It had learned that the people who succeeded in the past were mostly men, and it generalised. Defenders reply that humans do the same thing, only less consistently, and that a model can at least be audited. That is fair as far as it goes. A biased human cannot be inspected; a biased model can, at least in principle, and the inspection can be repeated by outsiders. The difficulty is that auditing requires knowing what to look for, and the companies best placed to audit are the ones selling the system. Until independent audits become routine — and until employers are required to publish what their systems measure — the promise of objectivity is likely to remain advertising rather than fact.

mk:cr-5.text: Every year the world produces more than 400 million tonnes of plastic, and only a small share of it is ever recycled. The figure that campaigners repeat most often is nine percent: the share of all plastic waste that has been recycled since the material became common in the 1950s. The number has barely moved in twenty years, even though recycling bins now stand in almost every kitchen in Europe and North America. Part of the explanation is technical. Plastics are not one material but thousands, and each type melts at a different temperature. A bottle and its cap, thrown in the same bin, may end up contaminating a whole batch. Sorting by hand is expensive, and machines that sort by colour or shape are easily confused by black plastic, which sensors cannot detect. A second explanation is economic. Recycled plastic competes with new plastic made from oil, and when oil is cheap, recycled material looks expensive. In 2020, the price of recycled plastic in Europe fell below the cost of collecting it, and several sorting plants closed. Governments responded with taxes on packaging, but manufacturers simply switched to paper, which is easier to recycle but heavier to transport. The industry's favoured answer is chemical recycling, in which plastic waste is broken down into oil-like substances and rebuilt. Supporters describe it as closing the loop. Critics reply that most of these plants run at low temperatures and produce fuel for burning, not new plastic, and that the process uses more energy than it saves. A recent review found that only three of the sixty plants operating worldwide produced material that could be used for food packaging. The more honest conclusion may be simpler. Recycling works best when there is less to recycle. Countries with deposit schemes and repair shops recycle far more than countries that rely on households to sort their own waste, not because their citizens are more careful, but because the system makes the easy choice the right one.

mk:cr-6.text: When offices reopened after the pandemic, many companies kept the option of working from home, and surveys suggested that most employees wanted it. The benefits are easy to list: no commute, fewer interruptions, and the freedom to arrange the day around school hours or medical appointments. But a growing body of research suggests that the costs are not shared equally. A study of 4,000 employees at a large technology firm tracked promotions over three years. Staff who worked fully remotely were promoted at roughly half the rate of those who came in three days a week, even after controlling for performance scores. The gap was widest for junior employees. The authors argue that promotion depends less on output than on what they call "proximity bias": managers reward people they see, remember and can imagine in a more senior role. Mentoring shows a similar pattern. In the same firm, junior staff who rarely came to the office reported having, on average, one significant conversation with a senior colleague per month, compared with four for those in the office most days. Those conversations are where young workers learn how decisions are actually made, which is rarely written down anywhere. Defenders of remote work point out that the study measures one company in one industry, and that the three-day group may simply have been more ambitious to begin with. They also note that remote arrangements can widen access for parents and disabled workers, groups that have historically been excluded from good jobs. The authors accept both criticisms, and say their conclusion is narrower than headlines suggest: it is not that remote work is bad, but that it cannot be offered as a neutral choice when the office still decides who gets ahead. Some firms have responded by fixing days rather than requiring attendance: everyone comes in on Tuesday and Thursday, and the rest is flexible. Early evidence suggests this hybrid pattern preserves much of the mentoring benefit without the daily commute.

Supporters argue that growing food close to where it is eaten [[01]] transport costs and gives consumers fresher produce. Critics, however, point out that the [[02]] of land in city centres makes large-scale farming impossible, and that soil on old industrial sites may be [[03]]. Most researchers agree that the movement is [[04]] to grow, but they warn against expecting it to [[05]] conventional agriculture. City gardens are far more likely to play a role in education. Children who [[06]] in planting vegetables are more willing to eat them, and teachers report a [[07]] in eating habits. For planners, the challenge is to [[08]] these projects without pushing up house prices — a risk that has already [[09]] in several neighbourhoods. The real [[10]], then, is not whether cities can grow food, but whether they can do it fairly.

Studies of eye movements show that people reading on a screen [[01]] far more quickly than they do on paper, and they are more likely to skip long paragraphs. This is not simply a matter of [[02]]. When a text is full of links and notifications, the brain keeps [[03]] for the next interruption, and deep attention becomes [[04]]. Publishers have responded by designing pages that [[05]] the reader's pace, but critics say such tricks cannot [[06]] for the loss of concentration. The [[07]] is not that screens are harmful, but that they invite a different kind of reading. Researchers suggest that students [[08]] serious texts on paper when the material is difficult, and reserve screens for material they only need to [[09]]. For most of the last century the public library was measured by one number: how many books went out through the door. That number has been falling for twenty years in almost every industrialised country, and no librarian now believes it will recover. Yet something unexpected has happened at the same time. Visits to library buildings have risen, in some cities by more than a third, even as borrowing has declined.
B

The explanation, according to a survey of 4,000 users, is that people come for the space rather than the shelves. A library is one of the few indoor places where a person can sit for six hours without buying anything. Students revise there, freelancers take calls there, and older residents come for warmth and company as much as for newspapers.
C

Responding to this shift, the city of Aarhus in Denmark rebuilt its main library in 2015 around what it calls the «third place» — neither home nor workplace. The building now contains a maker space with 3D printers, a recording studio, a kitchen where teenagers learn to cook, and a stage for local bands. Borrowing in Aarhus has continued to fall, but visits have doubled.
D

Not everyone is pleased. A letter signed by 200 residents complained that the reading rooms had become «a playground with books attached», and that the noise made concentration impossible. The head of the library service replied that the silence of the old building had also been a form of exclusion — many people had never felt entitled to walk in.
E

The compromise most libraries now adopt is zoning rather than choosing. Silent floors stay silent; the ground floor is deliberately noisy. Designers report that the single most requested feature is not a quiet room but a room where talking is allowed, because people who live alone often have nowhere else to speak.
F

What has changed most is the job itself. Librarians now spend less time stamping books and more time helping people judge whether a piece of information is trustworthy — a skill that has become urgent in an age of invented facts. Several library schools have rewritten their courses accordingly, and the profession's recruitment has begun to attract graduates who would once have gone into technology.
A

When offices closed in 2020, most companies assumed they had discovered a permanent efficiency. Employees saved two hours of commuting a day and reported higher satisfaction. Four years later the picture is more complicated: productivity has held up for routine tasks, but the informal conversations that generate new ideas have become rarer.
B

A study tracking 60,000 workers found that the number of «weak ties» — colleagues you know slightly — fell by about a quarter in fully remote teams. Weak ties matter because they are the channels through which information travels between departments. Teams that lost them were slower to adopt ideas that already existed elsewhere in the same company.
C

Managers, not surprisingly, are the group most attached to the office. Surveys consistently show that senior staff rate remote work far lower than their junior colleagues do, and that the gap widens with age. Critics point out that this is also the group whose careers were built face to face, and who therefore find it easiest to return.
D

Young employees tell a different story. For those in their first two years of work, the office is where they learn by overhearing — how a client is handled, how a proposal is really made. Several firms now report that junior staff who joined remotely are technically competent but struggle to negotiate internally.
E

The compromise emerging in many companies is neither full return nor full remote but a fixed pattern: two or three days together, chosen to overlap with the team rather than the individual. Attendance is no longer treated as loyalty. What matters is that the days are predictable, so that people who do come in actually meet the people they came to see.
F

Whether this settles the argument is unclear. The cost of office space is real, and so is the cost of a workforce that never learns to trust one another. Most executives now admit the question is not where people work but which tasks genuinely need to be done together — a distinction that few of them had to make before 2020.

When Maria, a retired teacher of seventy-two, first [[01]] a smartphone, she used it for one thing only: answering calls. Anything else seemed to require a password, an update, or a decision she did not feel able to make. Her experience is common. Surveys suggest that a large [[02]] of people over seventy own a smartphone but use only a small part of what it can do, and that many [[03]] to carry out tasks that younger users complete in seconds.

The reasons are not simply about skill. Designers often [[04]] that older users have weaker eyesight and shaky hands, so small buttons and low contrast make [[05]] difficult. Apps also change their layout without warning, which means that a routine learned in January may [[06]] by March. And help is rarely close at hand: many older people live alone, and a phone call to a busy child is not the same as a patient teacher sitting beside them.

Some cities have [[07]] the problem by pairing teenagers with older residents. In one programme, students spend two hours a week helping with banking, transport and video calls. The results are [[08]] : after three months, participants were twice as likely to use online services on their own, and the teenagers reported a [[09]] change in how they saw ageing.

None of this means that older people should be treated as a [[10]] group. Many learn quickly when the instructions match their habits, and the smartphone, used well, can reduce loneliness more than almost any other device.

Students often believe that time spent at a desk is the same as learning. Researchers who ask them to keep diaries find the opposite: long sessions are frequently broken by phone checks, and the last hour of a three-hour session produces almost nothing. Short sessions of twenty-five minutes, followed by a short break, keep attention high and are easier to repeat the next day.
B

Highlighting feels productive because the page becomes colourful, but studies that compare it with reading alone find little or no benefit. The reason is that marking a sentence does not require you to decide what it means. Summarising in your own words is far more effective, even though it feels slower and less satisfying.
C

Re-reading a chapter is the most popular revision method and one of the least effective. Familiarity is easily mistaken for knowledge: the text looks easy the second time, and the brain reads that ease as understanding. A closed-book test, which feels much worse, gives a far more accurate picture of what has actually been stored.
D

Many learners study one subject for weeks and then move to another, believing that this keeps the material fresh. Mixing two related topics within a single session produces more errors at the time and better results a month later, because the mind must keep choosing between methods rather than repeating one.
E

Sleep is often treated as the first thing to sacrifice before an exam. Yet the consolidation of new material happens largely during deep sleep, and students who shorten sleep by two hours remember less of what they studied the night before. Reviewing in the evening and sleeping normally outperforms staying up until two in the morning.
F

A final myth concerns ability. Learners who describe themselves as bad at a subject usually mean that they were once behind and never caught up. Studies of deliberate practice suggest that the gap between a beginner and an expert is explained mostly by the quality of practice, not by a fixed limit set at birth.

He travelled for a competition.
He could not sleep because of the noise.
mquestions.loc: I set my alarm for two in the morning, watched the whole thing, and we lost in the last five minutes.
mquestions.why: 男士说 set my alarm for two in the morning, watched the whole thing，整场看完才睡，所以疲惫的直接原因是熬夜看比赛。
on: 做项目是接下来的任务，不是昨晚没睡的原因。
正确项。
比赛是「看」不是「参加」，更没有出行。
原文没有提到噪音。
mquestions.tip: 长对话开头两句几乎必然交代「状态 + 原因」，把第一个 because 类信息记下来。
mquestions.pit: 把「今天要熬夜做 PPT」误当成「昨晚熬夜」的原因。
mquestions.unit: 长对话 · 校园互助

mquestions.st: What does the man still need to do for his presentation?
o: Collect the data.
Write the report.
Design the slides.
Book a lecture room.
mquestions.loc: Actually, the data's all there — it's the design that's killing me.
mquestions.why: the data's all there — it's the design that's killing me，数据齐了，卡在「设计」。
on: 数据 the data's all there，已经齐了，正是被否定的一项。
报告在对话中没有出现。
正确项，design 指幻灯片的设计排版。
订教室没有提到。
mquestions.tip: 破折号、but、actually 之后的短句，是长对话最爱出题的位置。
mquestions.pit: 听到 data 就选 A，忽略了 all there 是「已经完成」的意思。
mquestions.unit: 长对话 · 校园互助

mquestions.st: What does the woman offer to do?
o: Present the project for him.
Put his slides into the template.
Buy him lunch.
Check his data for errors.
mquestions.loc: If you send me the file, I can put it into the template we were given.
mquestions.why: 女士说 If you send me the file, I can put it into the template we were given，即帮他套用学校给的模板。
on: 她帮他做排版，但没有说要替他上台讲。
正确项。
咖啡是他请她（you can buy me coffee），方向反了。
数据本来就是对的，她也没提出要检查。
mquestions.tip: 记笔记时给每句话标上 W/M，避免张冠李戴。
mquestions.pit: 最后一句 you can buy me coffee 的主语是男士，选项故意把「谁请谁」调换。
mquestions.unit: 长对话 · 校园互助

mquestions.why: 1. D) cuts。主语是动名词短语 growing food close to where it is eaten（视为单数），谓语要用第三人称单数；语义上是「削减运输成本」。cut 与后文 gives 并列，时态一致。
mquestions.unit: 选词填空 · 城市农场

mquestions.why: 2. L) shortage。the ___ of land 需要名词，且与 impossible 呼应——市中心「土地短缺」才导致无法大规模种植。decline（下降）语义不合：土地数量下降不等于无法种植。
mquestions.unit: 选词填空 · 城市农场

mquestions.why: 3. B) contaminated。may be 后面接形容词或过去分词作表语；老工业用地的土壤「可能被污染」，与 may be unsafe 的逻辑一致。
mquestions.unit: 选词填空 · 城市农场

mquestions.why: 4. C) certain。be certain to do 是固定搭配「必定会」。此处说「这一趋势必定会继续扩大」，与后文 but they warn 形成让步。
mquestions.unit: 选词填空 · 城市农场

mquestions.why: 5. N) replace。expect it to ___ conventional agriculture，需要一个及物动词原形；replace 与后文 not whether cities can grow food 呼应。注意 decline 作动词是「拒绝」，语义不通。
mquestions.unit: 选词填空 · 城市农场

mquestions.why: 6. F) engage。engage in 是固定搭配「参与」。定语从句 Children who ___ in planting 缺谓语，且必须是原形复数一致的形式。
mquestions.unit: 选词填空 · 城市农场

mquestions.why: 7. K) a shift in eating habits。report a ___ in 需要名词；shift 指「转变」，与后文孩子更愿意吃蔬菜的结果对应。
mquestions.unit: 选词填空 · 城市农场

mquestions.why: 8. H) expand。to ___ these projects 需要动词原形，expand 表示「扩大规模」，与 without pushing up house prices 构成现实的张力。
mquestions.unit: 选词填空 · 城市农场

mquestions.why: 9. I) occurred。has already ___ 是现在完成时，必须填过去分词；occur 的过去分词 occurred（双写 r）。语义为「这种风险在若干街区已经出现」。
mquestions.unit: 选词填空 · 城市农场

mquestions.why: 10. J) question。The real ___ is not whether… but whether… 是典型的「真正的+名词」句式，question 表示「问题所在」。harvest 虽同为名词，但「真正的收获不是能否种菜」讲不通。
mquestions.unit: 选词填空 · 城市农场

mquestions.st: Fewer books are borrowed, but more people come into the buildings.
mquestions.loc: 定位 A 段：borrowing has declined 与 visits have risen 在同一段形成对照，题干用 fewer…but more 概括。
mquestions.why: 定位 A 段：borrowing has declined 与 visits have risen 在同一段形成对照，题干用 fewer…but more 概括。
mquestions.unit: 长篇阅读 · 图书馆的转型

mquestions.st: Some residents argued that the new design had destroyed the library's purpose.
mquestions.loc: D 段：200 位居民联名信称阅览室变成「附带图书的游乐场」，噪音使专注不可能——正是「destroyed its purpose」的改写。
mquestions.why: D 段：200 位居民联名信称阅览室变成「附带图书的游乐场」，噪音使专注不可能——正是「destroyed its purpose」的改写。
mquestions.unit: 长篇阅读 · 图书馆的转型

mquestions.st: The most valued feature is a space where conversation is permitted.
mquestions.loc: E 段：the single most requested feature is not a quiet room but a room where talking is allowed。注意题干把 most requested 提到句首，位置变了但意思没变。
mquestions.why: E 段：the single most requested feature is not a quiet room but a room where talking is allowed。注意题干把 most requested 提到句首，位置变了但意思没变。
mquestions.unit: 长篇阅读 · 图书馆的转型

mquestions.st: People use libraries partly because they can stay without spending money.
mquestions.loc: B 段：sit for six hours without buying anything。题干把 without buying anything 改写成 without spending money。
mquestions.why: B 段：sit for six hours without buying anything。题干把 without buying anything 改写成 without spending money。
mquestions.unit: 长篇阅读 · 图书馆的转型

mquestions.st: The staff's work has moved from handling books to judging information.
mquestions.loc: F 段：less time stamping books and more time helping people judge whether a piece of information is trustworthy。
mquestions.why: F 段：less time stamping books and more time helping people judge whether a piece of information is trustworthy。
mquestions.unit: 长篇阅读 · 图书馆的转型

mquestions.st: A city rebuilt its central library to serve purposes other than reading.
mquestions.loc: C 段：Aarhus 重建主馆，加入创客空间、录音棚、厨房与舞台——「serves purposes other than reading」。
mquestions.why: C 段：Aarhus 重建主馆，加入创客空间、录音棚、厨房与舞台——「serves purposes other than reading」。
mquestions.unit: 长篇阅读 · 图书馆的转型

mquestions.st: How does a mature tree reduce the temperature beneath it?
o: By absorbing heat into its trunk
By releasing water vapour and blocking sunlight
By improving the soil around its roots
By slowing the wind in the street
mquestions.loc: …simply by releasing water vapour through its leaves and by blocking sunlight before it reaches the ground.
mquestions.why: 第一段明确给出两个机制：releasing water vapour through its leaves 与 blocking sunlight before it reaches the ground。
on: 树干储热在原文没有出现，属于常识性但无据的推断。
正确项，两个手段都对上了。
土壤改善在全文未提及。
风的影响未提及。
mquestions.tip: 手段题数一数原文说了几个，选项少了或多了都要警惕。
mquestions.pit: 选项把两个真实手段拆开只留一个，或在后面加一个原文没有的手段。
mquestions.unit: 仔细阅读 · 城市树木的降温效应

mquestions.st: Why is planting trees difficult for city governments?
o: Residents usually oppose new trees in their streets.
Trees are too expensive to buy.
The benefits appear long after the political cycle ends.
Most cities have no space left for trees.
mquestions.loc: City budgets, however, are usually planned in four-year cycles… a gift to a mayor who will not be in office to open it.
mquestions.why: 第二段指出预算按四年周期编制，而一棵树要二三十年才「值得」，即收益出现在任期之后——这是原文给出的核心矛盾。
on: 原文没有居民反对新树；居民反对的是根把人行道顶坏（针对树种，不是种树本身）。
树苗本身不是主要成本，长成的时间才是难点。
正确项，「收益晚于政治周期」正是原文的因果。
原文没有说城市没地方种。
mquestions.tip: 问原因的题，回到原文找 because / which means / so 这类连接词后的句子。
mquestions.pit: 把第四段提到的「根顶坏人行道」误当成不种树的原因，其实那是对「快速树种」的批评。
mquestions.unit: 仔细阅读 · 城市树木的降温效应

mquestions.st: The word "mixed" in Paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.
o: combined from different sources
not completely good or bad
confused and unclear
shared by several cities
mquestions.loc: Fast growers…reach a useful size in a decade, yet they are also the first to drop branches in a storm…
mquestions.why: 后文紧接着说快生树种「十年成材，但最先在暴风雨中掉枝、根顶坏路面」，既有利也有弊，所以 results have been mixed 指「结果好坏参半」。
on: mixed 作「混合的」时确实有这个意思，但此处修饰 results，不是「混合来源」。
正确项，与前后的 yet 结构完全对应。
原文没有表达「混乱不清」。
与城市数量无关。
mquestions.tip: 词义题看标点：破折号、yet、but 之后往往是对该词的现场解释。
mquestions.pit: 按最常见的「混合」义项硬套，忽略 yet 之后列出的负面结果。
mquestions.unit: 仔细阅读 · 城市树木的降温效应

mquestions.st: What does the author suggest is most important?
o: Planting more trees as quickly as possible
Choosing fast-growing species
Counting the benefits of trees in financial terms
Giving each tree an email address
mquestions.loc: That change of accounting may matter more than any single planting programme.
mquestions.why: 最后一段第一句 That change of accounting may matter more than any single planting programme——作者明确把「把树的收益计入账目」排在所有种植计划之上。
on: 原文强调「种了不管会死」，数量不是重点。
快生树种被作者列为「结果参半」的尝试。
正确项，accounting 的同义是 counting benefits in financial terms。
给树开邮箱是墨尔本的具体做法，是例子不是结论。
mquestions.tip: 问「most important / main point」时，找含 more than / rather than / the real 的句子。
mquestions.pit: 把文中举的例子（邮箱、树种）当成作者的核心主张。
mquestions.unit: 仔细阅读 · 城市树木的降温效应

mquestions.st: What is the main reason so much edible food is thrown away?
o: Supermarkets sell food that is already old.
Shoppers misunderstand what the dates mean.
Food prices are too low to encourage care.
Fridges are often set at the wrong temperature.
mquestions.loc: The confusion is built into the language… Most shoppers do not know the difference.
mquestions.why: 第二段开头 The confusion is built into the language，全文的核心原因是消费者分不清 use by 与 best before 的含义。
on: 原文没有说超市卖即将过期的食品，只说日期被印得很晚。
正确项。
价格与冰箱温度都没有出现。
同上，无中生有。
mquestions.tip: 问 reason / why 时，锁定解释性段落，不要停在现象段。
mquestions.pit: 把第一段的现象（三分之一被扔）当成原因。
mquestions.unit: 仔细阅读 · 保质期标签与食物浪费

mquestions.st: What does the author say about "best before" dates?
o: They indicate that the food is no longer safe.
They are required by law for all packaged food.
They concern taste rather than safety.
They are used mainly by shop staff.
mquestions.loc: «Best before» is a quality date: the food is still safe afterwards, it simply may not taste as good.
mquestions.why: 原文 «Best before» is a quality date: the food is still safe afterwards, it simply may not taste as good，即管品质不管安全。
on: 「过期就不安全」是 use by 的含义，属于两者互换。
原文没有提法律强制。
正确项。
主要用于店员的是 display until，不是 best before。
mquestions.tip: 遇到两个易混概念，先在纸上各写一行定义，再对选项。
mquestions.pit: use by 与 best before 的定义被故意调换，这是本篇最核心的陷阱。
mquestions.unit: 仔细阅读 · 保质期标签与食物浪费

mquestions.st: Why do manufacturers add salt or remove water?
o: To make the food taste better
To allow a later date to be printed
To reduce the cost of production
To meet new government standards
mquestions.loc: …adding salt or removing water — to make those dates achievable.
mquestions.why: 原文 some adjust the recipe — adding salt or removing water — to make those dates achievable，目的是让印上去的日期能兑现，从而「保质期更长更好卖」。
on: 口味改变只是副作用，原文没说是为了更好吃。
正确项。
成本未被提及，加水/加盐与成本无关。
没有政府标准。
mquestions.tip: 目的题看 to / so as to / in order to 后面的不定式。
mquestions.pit: 把「加盐」理解为改善风味，忽略了破折号后的 to make those dates achievable。
mquestions.unit: 仔细阅读 · 保质期标签与食物浪费

mquestions.st: What can be inferred from the last paragraph?
o: Date labels should be abolished immediately.
Consumers should rely on their own senses.
Food past its date is always safe to eat.
Supermarkets should stop printing any dates.
mquestions.loc: The useful question is not «is it out of date?» but «does it look, smell and taste right?»
mquestions.why: 作者说日期是「为平均厨房写的规则，不是为你家的」；有用的问题不是「过期了吗」而是「看起来、闻起来、尝起来对不对」——即回到自己的感官判断。
on: 作者说的是「不能只靠标签」，没有主张立刻废除。
正确项，与 look, smell and taste 对应。
原文明确 use by 之后可能致病，不能说 always safe。
过于绝对，且与全文语气不符。
mquestions.tip: 推断题的正确项通常是「弱化表述」：should consider、may、tend to。
mquestions.pit: 推断题里出现 always / never / immediately 这类词，基本可以直接排除。
mquestions.unit: 仔细阅读 · 保质期标签与食物浪费

mquestions.st: 中国是茶的故乡。茶在中国人的日常生活中占有重要地位，客人来访时，主人通常会先沏一杯茶。中国茶主要分为绿茶、红茶和乌龙茶三大类，不同地区的人们偏爱不同的茶。近年来，越来越多的年轻人开始学习茶艺，他们认为泡茶不仅是一种技能，也是一种放松的方式。如今，中国茶已经传播到世界一百多个国家。
mquestions.ref: China is the homeland of tea. Tea plays an important role in the daily life of Chinese people: when guests arrive, the host usually makes a cup of tea first. Chinese tea falls mainly into three categories — green tea, black tea and oolong tea — and people in different regions prefer different kinds. In recent years, more and more young people have begun to learn the art of tea making, believing that making tea is not only a skill but also a way to relax. Today, Chinese tea has spread to more than one hundred countries around the world.
bd: 中国是茶的故乡 → China is the homeland of tea.（homeland 比 hometown 准确）
占有重要地位 → plays an important role in（固定搭配，别用 takes an important place）
主人通常会先沏一杯茶 → the host usually makes a cup of tea first（中文的「先」在英文放句末）
主要分为……三大类 → falls mainly into three categories（fall into categories 是标准搭配）
偏爱 → prefer（不必用 be fond of，prefer 更简洁）
泡茶不仅是一种技能，也是一种放松的方式 → not only… but also…（两种成分必须同词性：名词对名词）
传播到一百多个国家 → has spread to more than one hundred countries（现在完成时 + more than）
mquestions.unit: 翻译 · 中国茶文化

mquestions.st: Directions: Suppose your university library is collecting suggestions from students. Write a letter to the librarian to propose two improvements, explaining why each would help. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words. Do not sign your own name; use «Li Ming» instead.
mquestions.sample:
Dear Librarian,
I am a junior student in the School of Economics. Learning that the library is collecting suggestions from students, I would like to propose two improvements that I believe would benefit many of us.
First, it would be helpful if the reading rooms could stay open until midnight during the examination period. At present they close at ten, and many students who live in crowded dormitories have nowhere quiet to study after that hour; extending the opening time by two hours would make a real difference to our preparation. Second, you might consider introducing an online seat-booking system. Seats are often reserved by leaving a bag on the chair and then left empty for hours, which is frustrating for students who arrive early and find nothing available.
Thank you for taking the time to read this letter. I would be glad to offer further details if they would be of any use.
Yours sincerely,
Li Ming
outline: 第一段：说明身份与写信目的（library is asking for suggestions）
第二段：两条建议 + 各自理由（开放时间 / 座位预约或安静区）
第三段：礼貌收尾，期待回复
phrases: which would make a real difference to…
Thank you for taking the time to…
rubric: 格式（称呼 + 落款）不丢分
两条建议各带理由，内容完整
句式有变化，不只用一个 I suggest
无明显语法错误（时态、单复数、冠词）
mquestions.unit: 写作 · 建议信（校园服务）

mquestions.st: What did the study find about older adults who walked every day?
o: They were more likely to sleep well.
They were less likely to have memory problems.
They were 20 percent more active than others.
They recovered faster from heart disease.
mquestions.loc: …those who walked for at least 30 minutes a day were 20 percent less likely to develop memory problems over the following five years.
mquestions.why: 原文 those who walked for at least 30 minutes a day were 20 percent less likely to develop memory problems，结论就是「更不容易出现记忆问题」。
on: 睡眠在原文中根本没有出现。
正确项，less likely to develop memory problems 的同义表达。
20% 是「风险降低的幅度」，不是「活跃程度高出 20%」，属于把数字安错对象。
原文未提心脏病，也未提康复速度。
mquestions.tip: 听到百分比先问一句：这 20% 修饰的是谁？
mquestions.pit: 选项把 less likely 悄悄换成 more likely，或把 20% 挪到别的指标上。
mquestions.unit: 短篇新闻 · 健康研究

mquestions.ty: 原因细节 + rather than 结构
mquestions.st: According to the researchers, what may explain the effect?
o: The pleasure of exercising outdoors
Better blood flow to the brain
A healthier diet among walkers
Stronger social ties in the group
mquestions.loc: They say the effect may come from improved blood flow to the brain rather than from the exercise being enjoyable.
mquestions.why: 原文 the effect may come from improved blood flow to the brain rather than from the exercise being enjoyable，明确把「快乐感」排除，留下「脑部血流改善」。
on: exercise being enjoyable 正是被 rather than 否定的那一项。
正确项。
饮食与社交在原文都没有出现。
同上，属无中生有。
mquestions.tip: 听到 rather than / instead of / not…but，立刻在否定项旁打叉。
mquestions.pit: rather than 后面是被否定的一方，很多人只听到前半句就选了它。
mquestions.unit: 短篇新闻 · 健康研究

mquestions.st: What limitation of the study do the researchers mention?
o: The sample was too small.
It covered only one country.
It cannot prove cause and effect.
It lasted less than a year.
mquestions.loc: The team warns, however, that the study only shows an association and cannot prove that walking protects memory.
mquestions.why: 最后一句 warns…only shows an association and cannot prove that walking protects memory，即「只证明相关，不能证明因果」。
on: 样本是 12,000 人，恰恰是「样本很大」。
原文只提到瑞典的一所大学，但并未把「单一国家」当作局限说出来。
正确项，association ≠ causation 是研究类新闻的固定考点。
研究跟踪了 the following five years，不是「不到一年」。
mquestions.tip: 听到 however / warns / caution，后面 90% 是一道题，专记「不能证明什么」。
mquestions.pit: 选项用「样本小」「时间短」这类常识性缺陷去套，而原文并没有这么说。
mquestions.unit: 短篇新闻 · 健康研究

mquestions.st: What do the volunteers at repair cafés do?
o: Sell second-hand household goods.
Repair broken items for free.
Teach people how to sew.
Collect waste from local homes.
mquestions.loc: Visitors bring broken toasters, lamps, bicycles and clothes; the volunteers…try to fix them for free.
mquestions.why: 原文 Visitors bring broken toasters…the volunteers…try to fix them for free，核心功能就是免费修理。
on: 没有买卖，只有修理。
正确项。
缝纫机只是工具之一，教缝纫只是顺带，不是主旨。
不收垃圾，是居民把坏东西送过来。
mquestions.tip: 主旨题问的是「这件事整体在干什么」，不是「里面出现了什么」。
mquestions.pit: 把某个细节（用缝纫机）放大成整篇的主旨。
mquestions.unit: 短文听力 · 修理咖啡馆

mquestions.st: Where did the repair café movement begin?
o: Bristol
Amsterdam
Berlin
Copenhagen
mquestions.loc: …part of a movement that began in Amsterdam in 2009 and has since spread to more than 2,000 places worldwide.
mquestions.why: 原文 a movement that began in Amsterdam in 2009，起点是阿姆斯特丹；Bristol 只是文中举例的那一间。
on: Bristol 是这段报道的现场，不是运动的发源地。
正确项。
柏林未出现。
哥本哈根未出现。
mquestions.tip: 听到 began / originated / started in，立刻圈地点。
mquestions.pit: 报道的开头地点（现场）与运动的发源地是两个概念。
mquestions.unit: 短文听力 · 修理咖啡馆

mquestions.st: According to the organisers, what is the real value of repair cafés?
o: Reducing the amount of waste.
Saving money for local families.
The conversation and what people learn.
Training retired engineers.
mquestions.loc: The idea is not only to keep things out of landfill. Organisers say the real value is the conversation…
mquestions.why: 原文 The idea is not only to keep things out of landfill. Organisers say the real value is the conversation，明确把「减少垃圾」降级为附带效果。
on: 减少填埋正是 not only 那半句，属于被弱化的一项。
省钱在原文中没有被提及（虽然事实成立），属于合理但不合文的推断。
正确项，the conversation + people learn how their possessions work。
退休工程师是志愿者的来源，不是目的。
mquestions.tip: 听到 not only，先在 X 上打叉，再等真正的重点。
mquestions.pit: not only X but Y 中，X 常常就是最有诱惑力的错误选项。
mquestions.unit: 短文听力 · 修理咖啡馆

mquestions.why: 1. H) scroll。people reading on a screen 后缺谓语，主语复数用原形；scroll（滚动屏幕）与 far more quickly 搭配，描述屏幕阅读的行为方式。
mquestions.unit: 选词填空 · 屏幕阅读

mquestions.why: 2. D) habit。a matter of ___ 是固定结构「是……的问题」；此处说「这不只是习惯问题」，为后文「大脑机制」做铺垫。
mquestions.unit: 选词填空 · 屏幕阅读

mquestions.why: 3. K) waiting。keep doing 结构，需要 -ing 形式；keep waiting for the next interruption 表示「一直等着下一次被打断」。
mquestions.unit: 选词填空 · 屏幕阅读

mquestions.why: 4. B) difficult。becomes 后接形容词作表语；与前文 brain keeps waiting 形成因果——深度注意力变得「困难」。
mquestions.unit: 选词填空 · 屏幕阅读

mquestions.why: 5. J) slow。pages that ___ the reader's pace，从句缺谓语，先行词 pages 复数用原形；slow 作动词「放慢」，与前文阅读过快形成对照。
mquestions.unit: 选词填空 · 屏幕阅读

mquestions.why: 6. A) compensate。compensate for 固定搭配「弥补」；cannot compensate for the loss of concentration 语法与语义都成立。
mquestions.unit: 选词填空 · 屏幕阅读

mquestions.why: 7. F) point。The ___ is not that… but that… 是议论文常用的「要点句」；point 表示「要点」，与后文真正的观点对接。
mquestions.unit: 选词填空 · 屏幕阅读

mquestions.why: 8. O) read。suggest that students ___ serious texts 是虚拟语气（suggest 表建议），从句用动词原形；read 与 on paper 搭配。
mquestions.unit: 选词填空 · 屏幕阅读

mquestions.why: 9. I) skim。need to ___ 需要动词原形；skim 指「略读」，与前半句 serious texts…on paper 形成对照（重要的精读，轻松的略读）。
mquestions.unit: 选词填空 · 屏幕阅读

mquestions.why: 10. G) question。an open question 是固定表达「尚无定论的问题」，且 question 与句首 Whether 引导的主语从句呼应。
mquestions.unit: 选词填空 · 屏幕阅读

mquestions.st: Remote teams produced fewer new ideas because people stopped meeting colleagues outside their own group.
mquestions.loc: B 段：weak ties 减少四分之一，而 weak ties 是信息跨部门流动的通道；「outside their own group」即 weak ties 的改写。
mquestions.why: B 段：weak ties 减少四分之一，而 weak ties 是信息跨部门流动的通道；「outside their own group」即 weak ties 的改写。
mquestions.unit: 长篇阅读 · 远程办公的代价

mquestions.st: Senior managers tend to value the office more than younger staff do.
mquestions.loc: C 段：senior staff rate remote work far lower than their junior colleagues，题干把 lower rating 改写成 value more。
mquestions.why: C 段：senior staff rate remote work far lower than their junior colleagues，题干把 lower rating 改写成 value more。
mquestions.unit: 长篇阅读 · 远程办公的代价

mquestions.st: New employees find it harder to learn the unwritten rules of a workplace when they start online.
mquestions.loc: D 段：junior staff who joined remotely…struggle to negotiate internally；「unwritten rules」对应 learn by overhearing how a client is handled。
mquestions.why: D 段：junior staff who joined remotely…struggle to negotiate internally；「unwritten rules」对应 learn by overhearing how a client is handled。
mquestions.unit: 长篇阅读 · 远程办公的代价

mquestions.st: Companies are settling on a predictable weekly pattern rather than a fixed number of days.
mquestions.loc: E 段：fixed pattern…What matters is that the days are predictable。注意题干没有说「几天」，而是强调「可预期」。
mquestions.why: E 段：fixed pattern…What matters is that the days are predictable。注意题干没有说「几天」，而是强调「可预期」。
mquestions.unit: 长篇阅读 · 远程办公的代价

mquestions.st: The debate has shifted from location to which work needs to be done together.
mquestions.loc: F 段：the question is not where people work but which tasks genuinely need to be done together。
mquestions.why: F 段：the question is not where people work but which tasks genuinely need to be done together。
mquestions.unit: 长篇阅读 · 远程办公的代价

mquestions.st: What did the 2014 study find?
o: Laptop users remembered more facts than hand-writers.
Handwriting led to better performance on conceptual questions.
Students preferred writing by hand to typing.
Typing produced longer and better notes.
mquestions.loc: Laptop users wrote down far more words, but the handwritten group performed better on the conceptual questions.
mquestions.why: 原文 the handwritten group performed better on the conceptual questions，这是该研究最核心的结论。
on: 事实记忆方面原文并未说打字者更好（那是 2019 年综述的结论，且限于具体事实）。
正确项。
偏好问题原文没有调查。
原文说打字者写的字数更多，但没有评价「更好」。
mquestions.tip: 研究类文章里出现年份时，先分清每个年份对应哪一条结论。
mquestions.pit: 把 2019 年综述里的补充结论（事实类题目打字有优势）安到 2014 年的研究头上。
mquestions.unit: 仔细阅读 · 手写笔记与记忆

mquestions.st: What does the 2019 review suggest about the original finding?
o: It was completely wrong.
It applies only under certain conditions.
It was based on too few students.
It has never been repeated successfully.
mquestions.loc: …concluded that the original result was real but narrow. Handwriting helps when the material is conceptual…
mquestions.why: 原文 the original result was real but narrow，并给出范围：材料是概念性的、题目要求解释时才有效。
on: review 说 real，并没有说错误。
正确项，narrow 就是「有条件成立」。
样本量不是 review 的批评点。
replication 只是效果缩小或消失，不是「从未成功」。
mquestions.tip: but 后面的形容词才是作者真正的判断重心。
mquestions.pit: real but narrow 容易被读成「基本没用」。
mquestions.unit: 仔细阅读 · 手写笔记与记忆

mquestions.st: What point does the author make in Paragraph 4?
o: Students should be allowed to choose how they take notes.
The comparison may reflect practised habits rather than the tool itself.
Typing is more useful for most university courses.
Teachers should teach students to type faster.
mquestions.loc: What matters may not be the pen but the habit… Asking them to switch for one lecture measures a skill they have not developed…
mquestions.why: 第四段说「关键也许不是笔，而是习惯」：手写者练了多年总结，打字者练的是别的东西，临时切换测的是未训练的技能。
on: 作者没有主张让学生自选。
正确项。
作者没有说打字对多数课程更有用。
没有提教学建议。
mquestions.tip: 推断要贴着原文的句子走，多走一步就算错。
mquestions.pit: 看到「习惯重要」就顺势推出「应该尊重学生的选择」，这是原文没有的一步。
mquestions.unit: 仔细阅读 · 手写笔记与记忆

mquestions.st: What is the author's final advice?
o: Take notes by hand in every class.
Match your note-taking method to what you are learning.
Stop taking notes during lectures.
Use a laptop only for long lectures.
mquestions.loc: If you are learning a subject that requires you to explain ideas, slow down and write less. If you are collecting facts, speed is not a sin.
mquestions.why: 结尾两句话给出条件化建议：学需要解释的科目就放慢手写，收集事实就允许快。
on: 全文恰恰反对「一律手写」这条简单规则。
正确项。
作者从未建议不做笔记。
时长不是作者的判据。
mquestions.tip: 建议题看最后一段的条件句：if…, do… 就是作者的真实立场。
mquestions.pit: 被标题式结论（手写更好）带走，忽略末段的 but / if 条件。
mquestions.unit: 仔细阅读 · 手写笔记与记忆

mquestions.st: What assumption does the author question in Paragraph 2?
o: That human recruiters are always biased
That the words on a résumé are neutral
That software is cheaper than recruiters
That companies hire too few graduates
mquestions.loc: The argument contains a hidden assumption: that the words on the page are neutral. They are not.
mquestions.why: 第二段第一句 The argument contains a hidden assumption: that the words on the page are neutral. They are not. 作者质疑的正是「纸面上的文字是中立的」这一前提。
on: 作者并不否认人会有偏见，反而在后文承认（Defenders reply that humans do the same thing）。
正确项。
成本问题全文未讨论。
招聘数量未讨论。
mquestions.tip: 看到 They are not 这种短句否定，前面那句就是被攻击的靶子。
mquestions.pit: 把作者「承认」的观点当成作者「质疑」的观点。
mquestions.unit: 仔细阅读 · 算法招聘的偏见

mquestions.st: Why did the technology firm abandon its recruiting tool?
o: It was too expensive to maintain.
It rejected candidates from certain universities.
It penalised résumés that mentioned women's activities.
It could not handle a large number of applications.
mquestions.loc: …after discovering that it downgraded résumés containing the word «women's»…
mquestions.why: 原文 it downgraded résumés containing the word «women's», as in «women's chess club»——正是「压低含 women's 字样的简历」。
on: 成本未提及。
偏好某三所大学是第二段的一般性机制，不是这家公司弃用的原因。
正确项，downgrade = penalise。
处理能力未提及。
mquestions.tip: 举例段（for example / in 2018）的细节要和前一段的机制区分开。
mquestions.pit: 把第二段的「偏好某几所大学」当成第三段的例子。
mquestions.unit: 仔细阅读 · 算法招聘的偏见

mquestions.st: What is the author's attitude towards the defenders' argument?
o: Completely dismissive
Partly accepting but insufficient
Strongly supportive
Neutral and undecided
mquestions.loc: That is fair as far as it goes. A biased human cannot be inspected; a biased model can… The difficulty is that…
mquestions.why: 作者说 That is fair as far as it goes（在这一点上说得对），随后用 The difficulty is… 指出审计能力掌握在卖方手里这一根本问题，属于「部分认可但不够」。
on: 作者承认对方有一点道理（fair），不是完全否定。
正确项。
作者随后指出困难，不是强烈支持。
作者有明确立场，不是中立。
mquestions.tip: 抓 as far as it goes / up to a point 这类让步语，它们标记「半同意」。
mquestions.pit: 态度题只有四个档位时，「部分认可」这类中间态往往才是答案。
mquestions.unit: 仔细阅读 · 算法招聘的偏见

mquestions.st: What would make the promise of objectivity credible, according to the author?
o: Replacing algorithms with human recruiters
Routine independent audits and public disclosure
Training models on larger data sets
Asking candidates to remove personal details
mquestions.loc: Until independent audits become routine — and until employers are required to publish what their systems measure — the promise of objectivity is likely to remain advertising…
mquestions.why: 末段给出两个条件：independent audits become routine，以及 employers are required to publish what their systems measure。
on: 作者并未主张退回人工招聘。
正确项，两个条件都对上了。
数据量不是作者提出的解决办法。
匿名化简历在原文没有出现。
mquestions.tip: 遇到 Until… 句，把条件抄成清单，逐条对选项。
mquestions.pit: Until A and until B 是「除非」，容易被读成「在……之后才」，但条件内容必须两个都取。
mquestions.unit: 仔细阅读 · 算法招聘的偏见

mquestions.st: 中国高速铁路的发展速度令世界瞩目。目前，中国高铁运营里程超过四万公里，占全球高铁总里程的三分之二以上。高铁把许多原本需要一整天的旅程缩短到几个小时，使人们能够在一天之内往返于不同城市之间。高铁不仅方便了出行，也带动了沿线城市的经济发展。
mquestions.ref: The speed at which China's high-speed railway has developed has attracted worldwide attention. At present, the network covers more than 40,000 kilometres, accounting for over two thirds of the world's total. High-speed trains have shortened many journeys that once took a whole day to a few hours, making it possible for people to travel between cities and return within a single day. The railway has not only made travel more convenient but also boosted the economy of the cities along the lines.
bd: 发展速度令世界瞩目 → The speed at which… has attracted worldwide attention（介词 + which 引导定语从句，比 The development speed… is surprising 更稳）
运营里程超过四万公里 → the network covers more than 40,000 kilometres（cover 用于「覆盖里程」）
占……的三分之二以上 → accounting for over two thirds of…（现在分词作伴随状语）
把旅程缩短到几个小时 → shortened… to a few hours（shorten A to B，注意介词是 to）
使人们能够…… → making it possible for people to…（形式宾语 it 是加分结构）
带动经济发展 → boosted the economy（boost 比 improve 更贴切）
mquestions.unit: 翻译 · 中国高铁

mquestions.st: Directions: Some people believe that university students should take part-time jobs, while others argue that work distracts them from their studies. Write an essay of 120–180 words stating your opinion and giving reasons.
mquestions.sample:
Part-time work is often blamed for poor grades, but I believe the problem lies not in the job itself but in how it is managed. Students who work a reasonable number of hours usually gain more than they lose.
The clearest benefit is practice in managing time. A student who has to be at a café at seven in the evening learns to finish an essay in the afternoon rather than at midnight, and that habit tends to spread to other courses. Work also teaches something no lecture can: how to deal with a difficult customer, a late colleague or a mistake that costs money.
Admittedly, there is a real risk. Twenty hours a week on top of a full timetable leaves little room for reading, and some students do fall behind. Yet this is a problem of proportion rather than of principle, and it can be solved by limiting hours during examination periods.
In short, part-time work is neither a shortcut nor a trap. It helps those who can keep it in proportion, and harms those who cannot.
outline: 第一段：亮明立场（有条件地支持）
第二段：理由一（时间管理与社会经验）
第三段：理由二 + 让步（有风险，但可控）
phrases: the problem lies not in… but in…
a problem of proportion rather than of principle
neither a shortcut nor a trap
rubric: 立场清晰且具体（不是简单的「利弊兼有」）
两个理由有区分度，且带例子
让步段真实，不用来敷衍
结尾有升华或条件，不重复开头
mquestions.unit: 写作 · 议论文（兼职与学业）

mquestions.st: What is special about the new laboratory?
o: It is run by local companies.
Students design their own experiments.
It is open only to postgraduates.
It stores instruments donated by firms.
mquestions.loc: A university in Manchester has opened what it calls a student-run laboratory, where undergraduates design and carry out their own experiments instead of following set recipes.
mquestions.why: 首句就把特点说清了：student-run laboratory, where undergraduates design and carry out their own experiments instead of following set recipes。核心是「学生自己做实验设计」，不是「有个实验室」。
on: 原文说仪器是 local firms donated（企业捐赠），实验室并不是企业运营的。
正确项，与 design and carry out their own experiments 一一对应。
对象搞反了：使用者是 undergraduates（本科生），而且新计划还要把一年级学生也放进来。
former storeroom 是「原来的储藏室」，不是「存放仪器的仓库」，更不是实验室的特点。
mquestions.tip: 新闻首句里的同位语、定语从句往往是答案所在；把 who / where / instead of 后面的内容记下来。
mquestions.pit: 听到 donated by local firms、former storeroom 这类具体名词就以为抓到了特点，其实这些都是陪衬信息，题干问的是「特别之处」。
mquestions.unit: 短篇新闻 · 学生实验室

mquestions.st: According to the head of the chemistry department, what is the aim of the lab?
o: To publish more papers in student journals.
To train future researchers.
To teach students how to learn from failure.
To save money on laboratory equipment.
mquestions.loc: The head of the chemistry department says the aim is not to produce researchers but to teach students how to fail usefully.
mquestions.why: 原话是 the aim is not to produce researchers but to teach students how to fail usefully，not…but… 的重点在 but 之后：教学生「有价值地失败」。
on: 学生期刊发表 17 项是「结果」，不是办实验室的目的。
这正是被否定的那一半（not to produce researchers），听到就选会掉进 not…but… 的陷阱。
正确项：fail usefully 就是说「失败了也要能总结出东西」，后文的 short report explaining what went wrong 是它的具体做法。
省钱是副作用（second-hand instruments 二手仪器），原文没说这是目的。
mquestions.tip: 听到 not / rather than / instead of，笔尖停在后面那半句，答案八成在那儿。
mquestions.pit: not A but B 句型里，A 往往被读得又清楚又靠前，很多考生只记住了 A。
mquestions.unit: 短篇新闻 · 学生实验室

mquestions.st: What will the university do next September?
o: Close the original laboratory.
Raise the fee for using the lab.
Open a new lab for first-year students.
Replace all the second-hand instruments.
mquestions.loc: The university plans to open a second lab next September and to admit first-year students, a group that was previously excluded.
mquestions.why: 最后一句：plans to open a second lab next September and to admit first-year students, a group that was previously excluded。
on: 原文只说要再开一个，没有说要关掉原来的。
全文没有提费用，属于无中生有。
正确项：open a second lab + admit first-year students。
二手仪器是现有配置，没有说要全部更换。
mquestions.trap: 把「此前不包括」当「以后不包括」
mquestions.tip: 时间副词（next / previously / now）决定这句话是过去、现在还是将来，笔记里给动词加箭头。
mquestions.pit: previously excluded 说的是「过去不包括一年级」，容易被听成「以后也不包括」。
mquestions.unit: 短篇新闻 · 学生实验室

mquestions.st: Why does the student go to see Professor Lane?
o: To ask for a letter of recommendation.
To discuss a timetable clash and a dissertation topic.
To complain about the statistics class.
To ask for an extension of the deadline.
mquestions.loc: I am here about two things, if you have a minute. The research methods course clashes with my statistics class on Tuesday mornings. … The other thing is my dissertation.
mquestions.why: 开门见山：I am here about two things… The research methods course clashes with my statistics class… The other thing is my dissertation。两件事分别是课程冲突与论文选题。
on: 推荐信是后文导师主动提出的（I can write a letter），不是学生来访的目的。
正确项，概括了两条主线。
学生只是陈述冲突，没有抱怨课程质量。
截止日期是导师提醒的，学生没有申请延期。
mquestions.tip: 长对话第一句的 two things / I wonder if / I need to ask 就是场景标签，先记住数量再听细节。
mquestions.pit: 对话中后段出现 letter、deadline，容易被误当成来意。
mquestions.unit: 长对话 · 论文与选课

mquestions.st: What does Professor Lane suggest about the dissertation?
o: Writing about supermarkets in general.
Narrowing the topic to one store for four weeks.
Changing to a completely different subject.
Waiting until next term to start.
mquestions.loc: Pick one store, measure what it throws away for four weeks, and you will have something original.
mquestions.why: That topic is far too broad… Pick one store, measure what it throws away for four weeks, and you will have something original。
on: 这恰恰是被否定的方向（far too broad）。
正确项：限定一家店、连续四周称重记录。
导师没有要求换题，只要求缩小范围。
导师没有让推迟；相反给了本周五的期限。
mquestions.tip: 听到 too broad / too general / not specific enough，答案一定在「缩小范围」的具体动作里。
mquestions.pit: far too broad 说明原选题太大，选项 A 只是重复了学生原来的想法。
mquestions.unit: 长对话 · 论文与选课

mquestions.st: What will the professor do to help?
o: Speak to the store manager herself.
Write a letter for the student to get access.
Measure the waste together with the student.
Move the student into the Thursday group.
mquestions.loc: I can write a letter on department paper. That usually helps.

mquestions.why: 1. B) bought。空在 first 之后、a smartphone 之前，缺谓语动词，且后面 she used it 说明是「买了手机」；bought 是 buy 的过去式，与 used 时态一致。

mquestions.unit: 选词填空 · 老年人用手机

mquestions.why: 7. G) handle。have ___ the problem：现在完成时 have + 过去分词，handle the problem「处理问题」；与后文「请中学生结对」的具体做法呼应。

mquestions.why: 9. O) striking。a ___ change in how they saw ageing：表示「显著的变化」，striking change 是常见搭配；obvious 语意偏「显而易见」，程度不足。

mquestions.st: What does the figure of nine percent refer to?
o: The share of plastic waste recycled since the 1950s
The share of plastic burned in Europe
The share of packaging made of paper
The share of oil used to make plastic
mquestions.loc: The figure that campaigners repeat most often is nine percent: the share of all plastic waste that has been recycled since the material became common in the 1950s.
mquestions.why: 第一段直接定义：the share of all plastic waste that has been recycled since the material became common in the 1950s。
on: 正确项，与原文定义一致。
焚烧比例在第三、四段出现，但不是 9% 所指。
纸包装是第三段末尾提到的替代材料。

mquestions.st: Why is sorting plastic difficult according to the passage?
o: Because households refuse to wash their bins
Because plastics vary and sensors miss some types
Because there are too few recycling plants
Because paper is mixed with plastic
mquestions.loc: Plastics are not one material but thousands… machines that sort by colour or shape are easily confused by black plastic, which sensors cannot detect.
mquestions.why: 第二段给出两个原因：塑料种类多、熔点不同，且 machines that sort by colour or shape are easily confused by black plastic, which sensors cannot detect。
on: 原文没有提到居民不清洗回收桶。
正确项：种类繁多 + 传感器识别不了黑色塑料。
原文提到工厂关闭，但那是经济原因导致的，不是分拣难的原因。
纸是替代包装材料，与分拣难无直接因果。
mquestions.tip: 问 why 时只读带 because / the reason / part of the explanation 的句子。
mquestions.pit: several sorting plants closed 出现在第三段，属于「结果」而非「原因」。

mquestions.st: What is the critics' view of chemical recycling?
o: It produces high-quality food packaging.
It saves more energy than it consumes.
It often produces fuel rather than new plastic.
It has replaced mechanical recycling.
mquestions.loc: Critics reply that most of these plants run at low temperatures and produce fuel for burning, not new plastic, and that the process uses more energy than it saves.
mquestions.why: Critics reply that most of these plants… produce fuel for burning, not new plastic, and that the process uses more energy than it saves。
on: 只有 3/60 的工厂能产出食品级材料，与「高质量」相反。
原文说 uses more energy than it saves，方向相反。
正确项：多数产出的是燃料，不是新塑料。
化学回收是补充路线，原文没有说取代机械回收。
mquestions.tip: 看到 Supporters… Critics… 先标说话人，问谁的观点就只读谁那句。
mquestions.pit: Supporters describe it as closing the loop 是支持者的话，被放在前面，容易被当成作者态度。
mquestions.unit: 仔细阅读 · 塑料回收的真相

mquestions.st: What can be inferred from the last paragraph?
o: Households should sort waste more carefully.
System design matters more than individual effort.
Deposit schemes are too expensive for most countries.
Recycling should be abandoned altogether.
mquestions.loc: Countries with deposit schemes and repair shops recycle far more… not because their citizens are more careful, but because the system makes the easy choice the right one.
mquestions.why: 末段说：not because their citizens are more careful, but because the system makes the easy choice the right one，并强调 recycling works best when there is less to recycle。
on: 原文明确否定了「居民更细心」这个解释。
正确项：制度设计比个人努力更关键。
原文把押金制当正面例子，没有说太贵。
作者说 recycling works best when there is less to recycle，不是放弃回收。
mquestions.tip: 推理题优先找 not…but…、rather than、the more honest conclusion 这类评价句。
mquestions.pit: not because A, but because B 结构里，A 经常被误读成作者观点。

mquestions.st: What did the study of 4,000 employees find?
o: Remote staff were promoted about half as often.
Remote staff performed worse on scores.
Office staff worked longer hours.
Promotion rates were the same for both groups.
mquestions.loc: Staff who worked fully remotely were promoted at roughly half the rate of those who came in three days a week, even after controlling for performance scores.
mquestions.why: Staff who worked fully remotely were promoted at roughly half the rate of those who came in three days a week, even after controlling for performance scores。
on: 正确项：晋升率约为到岗组的一半。
原文是 after controlling for performance scores，说明绩效已被排除。
原文没有比较工作时长。
两组晋升率差异明显，不是相同。
mquestions.tip: rate / likelihood / chance 后面跟数字时，说的是比例不是人数。
mquestions.pit: half the rate 是「一半的速度」，容易被读成「一半的人」。

mquestions.st: What is "proximity bias"?
o: A preference for employees who are physically present
A rule that limits remote work to seniors
A tendency to promote the best performers
A system for measuring output online
mquestions.loc: …what they call "proximity bias": managers reward people they see, remember and can imagine in a more senior role.
mquestions.why: 原文自带解释：managers reward people they see, remember and can imagine in a more senior role，即「看得见的人更容易被提拔」。
on: 正确项：偏向「在身边、看得见」的员工。
原文没有限制远程资格的规则。
恰恰相反，bias 指的是偏离绩效的偏向。
这是管理心理，不是考核系统。
mquestions.tip: 生词 + 冒号/破折号/that is，后面十有八九是定义。
mquestions.pit: 不认识 proximity 时容易猜成「近似」「接近指标」，而忽略冒号后的解释。
mquestions.unit: 仔细阅读 · 远程办公的代价

mquestions.st: Why do defenders question the study?
o: It surveyed too few employees.
It covers one company and may reflect self-selection.
It ignored the cost of commuting.
It was funded by office landlords.
mquestions.loc: Defenders of remote work point out that the study measures one company in one industry, and that the three-day group may simply have been more ambitious to begin with.
mquestions.why: Defenders point out that the study measures one company in one industry, and that the three-day group may simply have been more ambitious to begin with。
on: 样本是 4,000 人，不算少，批评点在「一家公司、一个行业」。
正确项：样本范围窄 + 到岗组可能本身更有野心（自选择）。
通勤成本是远程办公的好处，不是对研究的质疑。
原文没有提资金来源。
mquestions.tip: 看到 point out that A, and that B，两个 that 都要读，题目常考第二个。
mquestions.pit: may simply have been more ambitious 是「自我选择」的说法，容易被漏掉，只记住「样本小」。

mquestions.st: What is the authors' conclusion?
o: Remote work should be banned for junior staff.
Remote work is harmful to all employees.
Remote work is not neutral while the office decides promotion.
Hybrid work has no benefits at all.
mquestions.loc: It is not that remote work is bad, but that it cannot be offered as a neutral choice when the office still decides who gets ahead.
mquestions.why: The authors accept both criticisms, and say their conclusion is narrower… it is not that remote work is bad, but that it cannot be offered as a neutral choice when the office still decides who gets ahead。
on: 作者没有主张禁止，只指出「不是中性的选择」。
原文明确 it is not that remote work is bad。
正确项：只要晋升仍由「到岗可见度」决定，远程就不是平等选项。
末段说 hybrid 保留了大部分指导收益，说明作者并不否定混合办公。
mquestions.tip: 看到 not that A, but that B，答案就在 B；同时留意 narrower than headlines suggest 这种降调表达。
mquestions.pit: 题目问 conclusion 时，正确项往往是「有限定的判断」，极端项一律排除。

mquestions.st: 近年来，许多中国城市修建了绿道，供市民步行和骑行。这些绿道大多沿着河流或旧铁路线修建，每隔几百米就设有休息点。绿道不仅为人们提供了锻炼的场所，也改善了城市的空气质量。如今，周末到绿道上散步已经成为许多家庭的习惯。
mquestions.ref: In recent years, many Chinese cities have built greenways for citizens to walk and cycle on. Most of these paths run along rivers or old railway lines, with rest areas every few hundred metres. Greenways not only provide places for people to exercise but also improve the air quality of the city. Today, walking on a greenway at the weekend has become a habit for many families.

供市民步行和骑行 → for citizens to walk and cycle on（介词 for + 名词 + 不定式；cycle on 的 on 不能丢，因为先行词是 paths）
沿着河流或旧铁路线 → run along rivers or old railway lines
每隔几百米设有休息点 → with rest areas every few hundred metres（with 复合结构）
不仅……也…… → not only… but also…，两侧都是动词原形

mquestions.st: Directions: It is common to see students checking their phones during lectures. Write an essay of 120–180 words analysing the causes of this phenomenon and suggesting possible solutions.
mquestions.sample:
Walk into a lecture hall of three hundred students and you will see dozens of screens glowing under the desks. Phone use in class has become normal enough that many teachers no longer comment on it.
Two causes stand out. The first is habit: students who check their phones every few minutes outside class do not switch off the reflex when they walk in, and a lecture offers plenty of moments that feel empty. The second is design. A ninety-minute monologue with no questions and no change of pace invites the mind to wander, and the phone is simply the nearest distraction.
The solution, therefore, cannot be scolding alone. Teachers could break long lectures into ten-minute segments with a question or a short task, which gives attention somewhere to go. Departments might also agree on a simple rule — phones face down on the desk — that is easy to check and does not require confrontation.
Attention is not a moral quality; it is a response to what is happening in the room.
outline: 第二段：两条原因（注意力习惯 / 课堂互动不足）
第三段：两条对策（课堂设计 / 明确规则）
phrases: a response to what is happening in the room
rubric: 原因分层（个人 + 环境）
结尾有观点而不是重复
mquestions.unit: 写作 · 现象分析（课堂上用手机）

mquestions.st: What does the rent cover?
o: Water and rubbish collection.
Electricity and heating.
Water and electricity.
Nothing but the flat itself.

By bus.
On foot.

mquestions.st: What is the talk mainly about?
